page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.i2g.2xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The instance is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB per core, and includes 959 GB of local SSD storage. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps, and virtualization is managed via the KVM hypervisor.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the ecs.i2g.2xlarge exhibits modest processing capabilities. In stress-ng tests, both single-core and multi-core CPU performance fall into the bottom 25% tier. Similarly, Geekbench scores reflect weak performance across single-core and multi-core workloads, including software compilation, ray tracing, and image processing. Memory bandwidth tests show a weak read-only large block throughput of 38.8 GB/sec, though large block write performance is average at 35.51 GB/sec. Passmark CPU tests place the instance in the middle 50% tier with a score of 7008.06, while database operations and Redis SET operations remain in the bottom 25%. Small LLM inference achieves average speeds of 445.76 tokens/second for prompt processing, but performance drops to poor levels with a medium 7B model.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.i2g.2xlarge offers a high local SSD storage density relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for workloads requiring substantial local storage without demanding high-performance CPU throughput. However, the tradeoff is its legacy processor architecture and lower benchmark-per-resource efficiency in compute-heavy tasks. This instance is best suited for general-purpose workloads, local file caching, lightweight database operations, and basic web serving where storage capacity is prioritized over high-speed processing.
